chunks: And in the narration of Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Manṣūr, he said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made an oath of abstinence from his wife, and then four months passed. He said: "He is to be detained; if he resolves upon divorce, she becomes separated from him, and she must observe the waiting period of a divorced woman. Otherwise, he must expiate his oath and retain her."

key_terms.آلَى: he swore an oath of abstinence from marital relations
key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ: the four-month period relevant to the ruling of īlāʾ
key_terms.الطَّلَاقَ: divorce as one of the two legal outcomes
key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: the waiting period observed by a divorced woman
key_terms.كَفَّرَ يَمِينَهُ: he must offer expiation for breaking his oath
key_terms.يُوقَفُ: he is made to stop and be brought to a binding decision

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man swears abstinence from his wife and four months pass?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on īlāʾ, when a husband swears abstinence from his wife. After four months, he is compelled to choose either divorce, which entails the divorced woman's ʿiddah, or expiation for his oath and continuation of the marriage.
